I'm Nathan, Elizabeth's older brother, and I've never seen her the way she was on Tuesday. She came home, dropped her bag in the hallway and went straight to her laptop. When I looked over her shoulder, she was typing a post about Anjali, something about Anjali's mum and the shop. Her jaw was tight and her hands were quick.
"She told everyone about me," she said without looking up. "So now everyone gets to know about her."
I don't know everything that happened between them. I just said, "Lizzie, can you wait till tomorrow? Right now you're the one who got hurt. Post that and you're the one who did the hurting."
She glared at me. Then she deleted the draft, blocked Anjali's number instead, and lay face-down on the sofa for an hour. I made her toast. I can't tell if she's angry or just really sad.

qa.q: What did Elizabeth do instead of posting?
qa.a: Elizabeth deleted the draft and blocked Anjali's number instead.

qa.q: Why did Elizabeth want to post about Anjali?
qa.a: Elizabeth was furious that Anjali told everyone about her and wanted Anjali to feel the same exposure.

qa.q: Why was waiting a day a wise suggestion?
qa.a: Anger that strong usually cools a little overnight; posting Anjali's secret would have made Elizabeth the one who did harm, while waiting keeps her choices open.

qa.q: How does Nathan see Elizabeth's evening?
qa.a: Nathan sees how upset his sister is but can't tell whether she is angry or deeply sad, so he stays near and makes her toast.

grounding: Shows a hurt teenage girl wanting to expose her friend's secret or cut her off, and a brother urging her to wait a day so she does not become the wrongdoer.

Monday: Urmila found out at lunch that Darshan had told the whole cricket group she still sleeps with a night lamp and hid in the storeroom during the last thunderstorm. By evening she had typed a message to the class group about Darshan's report card, the one his father tore up. Her thumb hovered over send.
Tuesday: She hadn't sent it. Her cousin Manu had said, "Sleep on it. If it's still right tomorrow, it'll still be right." In class she moved to the front bench and didn't look back once when Darshan said "Urmi". She felt cold, as if a door had slammed shut inside her.
Friday: The anger had cooled into something heavier. She deleted the draft. She still wasn't talking to Darshan. But she was glad the story about the report card was still his to tell.

qa.q: What did Darshan tell the cricket group about Urmila?
qa.a: Darshan told them she still sleeps with a night lamp and hid in the storeroom during the last thunderstorm.

qa.q: How was Urmila feeling on Tuesday, and what shows it?
qa.a: Urmila felt cold and shut off; she moved to the front bench and didn't look back when Darshan called her 'Urmi'.

qa.q: How did waiting help Urmila avoid a mistake?
qa.a: Sleeping on it let the anger cool, so Urmila deleted the draft instead of exposing Darshan's secret and becoming the one in the wrong.

qa.q: What would change for Darshan if Urmila had sent the message on Monday?
qa.a: Darshan's private pain about the report card would have been exposed, and the story would shift from what Darshan did to what Urmila did.

grounding: Illustrates a teen's urge to retaliate by exposing a friend's secret and her withdrawal, with waiting a day keeping her on the right side of the story.

Kamal, you asked what to do about the boy who told your secret. Let me tell you what your Binita bua did at your age.

My friend Radha told the whole class about my father's drinking. I came home burning. I knew a secret of hers too: she had copied in the final exam. I could have told the teacher the next morning. I had even written a note.

My grandmother saw me writing. She didn't take the paper. She only said, "Sleep first. Decide tomorrow."

I was furious with her too. But I slept. And in the morning, I saw it clearly: if I told, the story would be about my revenge, not about what Radha did to me.

I tore up the note. I stopped sitting with Radha, and I didn't pretend it was fine. But I didn't become her.

qa.q: What secret did Binita know about Radha?
qa.a: That Radha had copied in the final exam.

qa.q: What did Binita feel coming home after Radha told the class?
qa.a: Binita felt furious and humiliated, burning with the urge to take revenge.

qa.q: What turning point in the story changed what Binita did?
qa.a: Her grandmother's advice to sleep first and decide tomorrow; waiting a night let Binita see revenge would make her the one in the wrong.

qa.q: How might Radha have experienced Binita's silence afterwards?
qa.a: She may have felt uneasy and guilty, noticing Binita had stopped sitting with her without any public fight.

grounding: Binita bua recalls wanting to expose her friend's secret in revenge, and how waiting a day kept her from being on the wrong side of the story.

The school trip bus to Mysuru broke down on the highway, and for three hours Aadhya had to sit two rows behind Ayesha, the friend who had told everyone about her panic in the exam hall.

Aadhya's phone was in her hand. She had the group chat open. She knew about Ayesha's shoplifting dare in Class 7; one message and everyone would know that too.

She typed half of it. Her thumb hovered.

Beside her, Dimple was asleep against the window. Up front, Ayesha was laughing with the new girls as if nothing had happened.

Aadhya's jaw ached from clenching. She wanted Ayesha to feel exactly what she had felt.

She deleted the message, then muted Ayesha's name. Not forgiveness; just not tonight. Tomorrow she would decide whether to talk to her or walk away. Tonight, she put in her earphones and watched the lorries pass.

qa.q: How long did the bus sit broken down?
qa.a: Three hours.

qa.q: How can you tell Aadhya is angry?
qa.a: Her jaw aches from clenching and she types half a revenge message; she feels furious and wants Ayesha to feel the same humiliation.

qa.q: Was deleting the message a wise choice, and why?
qa.a: Yes; waiting a day stops her from exposing a secret in anger and becoming the one in the wrong, while she can still decide calmly tomorrow.

qa.q: How might Ayesha have felt if the shoplifting dare had been posted?
qa.a: She would likely have felt exposed and humiliated, and Aadhya would then share the blame for spreading a secret.

grounding: On a stranded school bus, Aadhya wants to expose her friend's secret or cut her off, but chooses to wait a day before deciding.

passage:
Keerthana sat on the staircase of her apartment block in Chennai, still in her school uniform, scrolling through Noor's profile. Every photo of the two of them made her feel sick now.

Three days ago Noor had told the boys in their class about the letter Keerthana wrote and never sent. Now they recited lines from it in the corridor.

Keerthana knew about Noor's failed maths test, the one Noor had hidden from her parents. She had Noor's aunt's number. One call.

Her cousin Deepak came down the stairs and found her there. "You look like you want to set something on fire."

"Maybe I do."

He sat beside her. "Whatever it is, do it tomorrow. If you still want to."

She put the phone face down. She would unfollow Noor today, which felt right. Everything else could wait until morning, when she wasn't shaking.

qa.q: What did Noor tell the boys in the class about?
qa.a: The letter Keerthana wrote and never sent.

qa.q: Why does Keerthana think about calling Noor's aunt?
qa.a: She feels angry and humiliated and wants revenge, to make Noor feel exposed too.

qa.q: What did Deepak's advice help Keerthana see?
qa.a: That waiting until tomorrow could stop her from acting while shaking with anger, since revenge would put her in the wrong.

qa.q: What would change for Noor if Keerthana called the aunt?
qa.a: Noor would face trouble at home and feel betrayed, and Keerthana would become the one who spread a secret.

grounding: Keerthana wants to expose Noor's secret after being betrayed, but chooses to wait a day and only unfollow her for now.

"I'm going to post it, Didi. Keerthana told everyone about my crush. So I'll tell everyone what she did at Diwali."

Ishita was sitting on her bed with her phone, thumbs already moving.

Roshni didi took the phone gently out of her hand. "What did she do at Diwali?"

"Doesn't matter. Something she'd hate people knowing."

"And then what?"

"Then she'll know how it feels."

"And everyone will know two secrets instead of one. And tomorrow people will be talking about what you did, not what she did."

Ishita pulled her knees up. "So I just let her get away with it?"

"No. You wait one day. Tomorrow you decide: talk to her, or stop being friends. Either is fine. Just not tonight, when you're this angry."

Ishita stared at the ceiling. "I hate that you're right."

"I'll give your phone back at breakfast," said Roshni.

qa.q: What did Keerthana tell everyone?
qa.a: Keerthana told everyone about Ishita's crush.

qa.q: What was Ishita feeling as she started typing the post?
qa.a: She felt furious and hurt, wanting Keerthana to feel the same humiliation.

qa.q: Why was waiting one day the wise move?
qa.a: Posting Keerthana's secret would have made Ishita the one in the wrong; waiting lets her choose calmly whether to talk or end the friendship.

qa.q: How might Roshni didi be feeling in this conversation?
qa.a: Roshni is probably protective and concerned, wanting to stop Ishita from doing something she'd regret.

grounding: A teen wants revenge by exposing her friend's secret, and an older sister helps her wait a day instead.
